html:
SMTO-GWT-0086 — The Gateway's saved job records failed a safety check

GUID: 62a6fc20-63bd-50e3-893c-c99816476d81
Slug: gateway-recovery-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • The Gateway keeps records of the jobs it has run. While loading, backing up or restoring those records, one didn't pass a safety check, so the Gateway won't use them. A destination problem doesn't mean the records are damaged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were making a backup or restoring one, choose a new folder that doesn't exist yet as the destination, then run it again. The backup and restore tools never write into an existing folder, so a used folder name is refused.
  2. If the Gateway refuses to start, leave it stopped and don't delete, move or edit anything in its data folder. Those records are how the Gateway knows which jobs already ran; losing them could make work run twice.
  3. Open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The exact message tells the person fixing it which record or folder failed the check.

What success looks like

  • The backup or restore finishes and prints its result, or the Gateway starts and shows as connected in Settings › Setup › Gateways.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't delete the Gateway's data folder or its old backups, and don't rerun jobs whose results you can't confirm.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway state recovery or the offline backup/restore tool rejected the saved state or its destination: invalid identity or format, checksum or receipt proof, contradictory outcomes, a linked or changed backup entry, or a destination that already exists.

What this means

  • Recovery or backup checks rejected invalid identity/schema, checksum or receipt proof, contradictory outcomes, unsafe backup entries, changed source files or an existing destination. An invalid destination is not proof that the checkpoint is corrupt. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Recovery or backup checks rejected invalid identity/schema, checksum or receipt proof, contradictory outcomes, unsafe backup entries, changed source files or an existing destination. An invalid destination is not proof that the checkpoint is corrupt.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the exact failing check and whether it concerns the source checkpoint, a receipt or the requested backup/restore destination; preserve originals.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact message (for example "Backup destination must not exist", "Invalid bundle or existing restore destination", "Gateway backup source changed", "Invalid Gateway terminal receipt"). For a destination error, rerun python -m gateway_core.runtime_state backup (or restore) with the Gateway state root and a new, non-existent --destination; for invalid saved state, stop the Gateway, wait for workers to finish, preserve the jobs root and fences, and use python -m gateway_core.runtime_state inspect or validate (and previous only by explicit choice) as described in docs/gateway-ram-first-operations.md.
  • Preserve checkpoints and emergency receipts. For a destination error, choose a valid new destination; for invalid saved state, drain the Gateway and use supported offline inspection and repair.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported offline inspection validates source evidence and a safe destination before recovery proceeds.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
